soil_type: Clayey, caliche-influenced soils over limestone; sits on the Balcones Escarpment transition zone with stratified profiles of limestone near pockets of volatile clay.
soil_leak_note: Clay pockets expand in rain and shrink in drought, pulling away from slabs and stressing buried pipes; limestone areas are stable but clay-filled seams and placed fill move, causing differential settling and pipe breaks.
foundation_types: Slab-on-grade dominates in the 2000s+ suburbs; pier-and-beam in older/Hill Country hillside areas.
housing_era: Historic downtown core (German-settled 1840s) plus heavy 2000s–2020s suburban growth.
common_pipe_materials: Pre-1980: galvanized steel and cast iron; 1980s–90s: copper and PVC; 2000s+: PEX.

housing_era: Historic downtown (Hill Country Mile) plus 2000s–2020s upscale suburban growth.

soil_type: Texas Blackland Prairie: deep dark-gray to black alkaline clays (Houston Black clay series), vertisols with very high shrink-swell potential.
soil_leak_note: These 'cracking clays' shrink and form deep cracks in dry weather and swell forcefully when wet, acting like a hydraulic pump under slabs — the leading driver of slab leaks and pipe shear in the area.
foundation_types: Slab-on-grade dominates; some pier-and-beam in older sections.
housing_era: 1990s–2010s suburban boom with continued master-planned growth (Homestead, The Crossvine, etc.).
common_pipe_materials: Pre-1980: galvanized steel and cast iron; 1980s–90s: copper and PVC; 2000s+: PEX.
